title: Closeouts
lead: Who closes out, how (run, speed, timing, angle), what the ball handler does next, and how that depends on his shooting and driving.

blocks.text: A closeout is a defender running at a player who has just caught the ball. It is a trade: close tight and fast and he may drive past you; stay back and he may shoot. This tab describes SkillCorner's closeouts in the ten games: the defender's run from the tracking, what the ball handler did next, and how that depends on what kind of player he is.

blocks.title: Where the closed-out player caught the ball

blocks.text: About 60 closeouts per game means most defenders have a handful. Rates per defender are shown with their counts and should be read as descriptions of these games, not ratings.

blocks.title: The chance's outcome by the ball handler's action

blocks.text: How tight, how fast and how early the defender arrived, from SkillCorner's end distance and the tracking. Each panel shows the next action and the chance's points.

sections.title: What this shows and does not

blocks.text: It shows how closeouts are run in these games and what follows them, split by the defender's run and by the kind of player closed out on. It does not grade defenders: most have under ten closeouts, the player they close out on drives the outcome, and SkillCorner's closeout detection itself is not validated here.

If this becomes the topic: a closeout value = outcome after the closeout minus what that ball handler usually produces from the same spot (season and tracked priors), pooled per defender with shrinkage; then separate the run (speed, angle, timing) from the result.
